name: Source Code to AI Baseline
description: Blocks uploads of source code to AI/ML applications, detecting 13 languages (C#, C++, Go, HTML, Java, JavaScript, Kotlin, Python, Rust, SQL, Swift, TypeScript, VB.NET) with the v4.14 Source Code DLP pattern library. Each language is two dictionaries joined with All (AND) in one engine: an Anchor (one structural fingerprint, threshold > 0) and a Signal (eight syntax patterns counted as unique matches, count threshold), so a file triggers only when the language's fingerprint is present AND enough language-specific evidence accumulates. That composition removes the cousin-language false positives (Java/Kotlin, C#/VB, JavaScript/TypeScript) the old three-dictionary ZBP set produced. The rule's application scope is resolved from the tenant's AI_ML cloud-application catalogue at deploy time. Immutable: objects that drift from this definition are restored. The rule's action is BLOCK, so enable it only after tuning in a pilot scope. All rules ship DISABLED at INFO severity (Zscaler's delivery convention): review, tune, then enable each rule and raise its severity.
source: DLP Pattern Library v4.14 (per-pattern descriptions with regex); rules from mkoyfman/zbp-automation zbp-source-code-dlp-zia
references: Zscaler Best Practices: Data Protection for Generative AI
Zscaler: About DLP Engines (All / Any operators)
notes: Regenerate from a new library version with: python tools/pack_from_pattern_doc.py <descriptions.docx> --pack zbp_source_code_baseline, then python pack_terraform.py zbp_source_code_baseline --out terraform.

Signal thresholds: > 4 unique matches for every language, > 3 for HTML (its structure is constrained, per the library notes). Change --threshold / --html-threshold when regenerating if the specification document sets different counts.

The three ZBP dictionaries and engines this pack used to ship (ZBP-Python/JavaScript/Shell Code Detection) are gone. A tenant that has them from an earlier deploy keeps them; delete them in the portal or undo that deployment, they are no longer referenced by any rule of this pack.

Patterns use (?m) line anchors and non-capturing groups, which ZIA's PCRE accepts; none uses lookaround. Every pattern is within ZIA's 256-byte limit and every Signal dictionary has exactly eight patterns (the ZIA maximum).
audience: Engineering-heavy organisations that worry about source code being pasted or uploaded into AI tools.
when_to_use: The customer wants to stop source code in any of 13 languages reaching AI/ML applications with near-zero cousin-language false positives. The rule is BLOCK once enabled, so pilot it with a small group first.
